los.text: Perform a neurological examination of the upper limbs with a structured and systematic approach
los.html:
• Session: lower limb neurological examination (the spreadsheet wording says upper limbs).
StepDetail
GaitSpastic, high-stepping (foot drop), ataxic, shuffling (Parkinson's), waddling; Romberg's (sensory ataxia)
InspectionWasting, fasciculation, scars, deformity (pes cavus)
ToneLeg roll, knee lift, ankle clonus (>3 beats = UMN)
PowerHip flexion (L2/3), extension (L4/5), knee extension (L3/4), flexion (L5/S1), ankle dorsiflexion (L4/5), plantarflexion (S1/2), big toe extension (L5)
ReflexesKnee (L3/4), ankle (S1/2), plantar (upgoing = Babinski: UMN)
CoordinationHeel–shin test
SensationDermatomes (L4 medial leg, L5 dorsum of foot, S1 lateral foot), vibration, proprioception (start at the big toe)
  • Patterns: UMN (stroke, cord compression)
    • LMN (root, peripheral nerve)
    • peripheral neuropathy (glove and stocking, absent ankle jerks)
    • cauda equina (saddle anaesthesia, retention, reduced tone).

los.text: Demonstrate the correct technique for conducting a clinical examination of the lumbar spine, identifying relevant anatomical landmarks and interpreting key physical findings.
los.html:
StepDetail
LookPosture: lordosis, kyphosis, scoliosis, muscle spasm, scars
FeelSpinous processes, paraspinal muscles, sacroiliac joints; landmarks: iliac crests at L4
Move
  • Flexion (Schober's test: mark 10 cm above and 5 cm below the dimples of Venus; should increase by >5 cm on flexion), extension, lateral flexion
  • Rotation is thoracic
Special testsStraight leg raise (pain down the leg at 30–70° = L5/S1 root irritation, sciatica); femoral stretch (prone knee flexion: L2–4)
NeurologyLower limb myotomes, dermatomes, reflexes
  • Red flags: age >50 or <20 with new pain
    • cancer history
    • weight loss
    • fever
    • IV drug use
    • trauma
    • osteoporosis
    • cauda equina symptoms
    • progressive neurological deficit.

los.text: Perform a comprehensive cardiovascular examination within 8 minutes, and provide structured feedback on the findings, demonstrating the ability to efficiently assess and communicate clinical information.
los.html:
CVS in 8 minutes: priorities
Brief intro, consent, positioning (30 s)
General inspection and hands with pulse (1 min)
Face, neck: JVP and carotid (1 min)
Apex beat, heaves, thrills (1 min)
Auscultation of 4 areas + manoeuvres (2 min)
Lung bases, ankle/sacral oedema (1 min)
State finishing steps (BP, peripheral pulses, ECG, fundi, urine dip) and present (1 min)
  • Structured feedback: what went well, what to improve, one specific action.

los.text: Perform a comprehensive respiratory examination within 8 minutes, and provide structured feedback on the findings, demonstrating the ability to efficiently assess and communicate clinical information.
los.html:
Respiratory in 8 minutes
Intro, positioning, inspection (around the bed)
Hands (clubbing, flap), pulse, respiratory rate
Face, neck (trachea, nodes)
Front: expansion, percussion, auscultation, vocal resonance
Back: the same, efficiently
Oedema; finishing steps (sats, PEFR, sputum, CXR); present

los.text: Perform a comprehensive gastrointestinal examination within 8 minutes, and provide structured feedback on the findings, demonstrating the ability to efficiently assess and communicate clinical information.
los.html:
GI in 8 minutes
Intro, lie flat, expose, inspect
Hands (clubbing, leuconychia, palmar erythema, flap)
Face (jaundice, pallor), neck (Virchow's node), chest (spider naevi, gynaecomastia)
Palpate: light, deep, liver, spleen, kidneys, aorta
Percuss: liver, spleen, shifting dullness
Auscultate
Finishing steps (hernial orifices, genitalia, DRE, urine dip) and present
